one_liner: Air Force headquarters program manager planning and coordinating violence-prevention and resilience programs (sexual assault, suicide, domestic violence) and managing related contracts at the Pentagon.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship-building and government-client consulting at IEM fit the coordination, legislation-tracking and briefing parts of this job. However, every grade requires a year of specialized experience in interpersonal and self-directed violence (ISDV) prevention work such as sexual assault prevention, domestic violence, child maltreatment, workplace violence or suicide, which nothing on file shows. Emergency management alone is unlikely to qualify unless the IEM work touched these areas.
eligibility: Open to the public under Direct Hiring Authority for Prevention Workforce positions; no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.

Specialized experience: one year at the next-lower grade (e.g., GS-07 level for GS-09) in ISDV program work: sexual assault prevention and response, domestic violence, child maltreatment, workplace violence, or suicide.
Education substitute: two years of graduate study or a master's degree qualifies for GS-09, and a Ph.D.-level program for GS-11. Transcripts are required if you rely on education.
No security clearance is required. The job is on-site at the Pentagon with no telework.
Part-time, unpaid and volunteer experience counts if your resume shows the duties and hours per week.
strategy: Start with an honest check: did any IEM project, volunteer role (crisis hotline, victim advocacy, suicide-prevention outreach) or coursework involve ISDV prevention? If not, this posting is a long shot, so apply only as a low-cost try and focus on better-matched roles.
If you have a master's degree or two years of graduate study, apply at GS-09 on education and upload transcripts. This may be your most realistic path in.

Frame IEM work around crisis-action planning, preparedness and resilience, coordination with multiple government stakeholders, and contract and cost support, using the posting's wording only where it truly applies.
Show your policy strength as tracking legislation and turning it into program goals and guidance, which mirrors the duty 'develop goals and objectives based on new and revised legislation.'
Answer the questionnaire truthfully and only at levels your two-page resume proves. Mismatches lead to a 'not qualified' rating.
The posting stays open until June 26, 2027, but direct-hire announcements often refer applicants in batches, so apply early. List exact dates and hours per week for each job.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [preparedness/resilience planning] for [number] [federal/state/local] government clients, building coordination mechanisms across [agencies/offices] to meet [program objective].
Analyzed [new legislation/regulation, e.g., Stafford Act changes] and drafted [guidance/briefings] with options and recommendations for [client leadership level].
Supported [single/multi-year] contract of $[value] by [forecasting cost/tracking deliverables/managing schedule], achieving [result, if known].
interview_questions: Describe your experience with sexual assault prevention, suicide prevention, or other ISDV programs.
Tell us about a time you balanced competing priorities among several internal and external stakeholders.
How would you turn new legislation into program guidance for installations and major commands?
Describe a briefing where you presented options and recommendations to senior leaders on a controversial issue.
watch_outs: The ISDV specialized-experience requirement applies at every grade, so without it you can qualify only through graduate education at GS-09 or GS-11.
The job is fully on-site at the Pentagon with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
The posting covers GS-9 through GS-15, but your realistic entry grade is likely GS-09 at about $52,727 unless you have documented ISDV experience.
